title: Vietnamese Chicken Vermicelli Bowl

extendedIngredients.name: lemongrass
extendedIngredients.original: 2 lemongrass stalks, white part only, finely chopped

extendedIngredients.name: fish sauce
extendedIngredients.original: 100 ml fish sauce (2 tbsp for the marinade, 3 tbsp for the sauce)

steps: Finely chop the lemongrass and crush 2 garlic cloves. Mix in a large bowl with 2 tbsp of the fish sauce, 2 tbsp of the brown sugar and a splash of olive oil. Add the chicken thigh fillets and turn to coat. Marinate for at least 15 minutes, or up to overnight in the fridge for the best flavour.

Make the nuoc cham dressing: crush the remaining 2 garlic cloves and stir together with the remaining 3 tbsp fish sauce, the juice of 2 limes, the rice vinegar, the remaining 2 tbsp brown sugar, the sliced chilli and 125 ml water. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then set aside so the flavours meld.
Cook the rice vermicelli noodles according to the packet directions. Rinse under cold water to stop them sticking, then drain well.
Julienne the carrots and cucumbers, finely shred the iceberg lettuce, and pick the mint and coriander leaves.
Heat a chargrill pan or barbecue over high heat until very hot. Cook the chicken for about 5 minutes each side until deeply caramelised and cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Divide the noodles between 4 bowls. Arrange the lettuce, carrot and cucumber around the noodles, scatter over the mint and coriander, and top with the sliced chicken.
Cut the remaining lime into wedges. Drizzle the nuoc cham generously over each bowl and serve with the lime wedges.
